paper_summary: Pados et al. produced AlSi7Mg aluminium matrix syntactic foams (MMSFs) by pressurised (500 kPa argon) infiltration of Liapor lightweight expanded clay aggregate particles (LECAPs, sieved to 2.5-3.0 mm), then machined ~26 mm diameter, 160 mm long cores and either left them bare, inserted them into heat-treated AlMgSi0.5 tubes (32 mm OD, 2 mm wall), or adhesively bonded them into the tubes with 3M Scotch-Weld DP410 epoxy. Quasi-static three-point bend tests (ISO 7438:2020, 140 mm span, 5 mm/min) up to 25 mm deflection showed flexural strengths of 69 MPa (bare MMSF), 159 MPa (foam-filled tube) and 169 MPa (adhesive-bonded foam-filled tube), i.e. the epoxy-bonded tubes gained 6% over unbonded foam-filled tubes and 145% over bare MMSFs. The foam cores had an average density of 1.48 +/- 0.05 g/cm3, roughly half that of the aluminium alloy.

structure.microstructure_notes: Study-wide average foam density 1.48 +/- 0.05 g/cm3. The two bare MMSF bend specimens had individual densities of 1.42 and 1.60 g/cm3 (Table 1, both labelled MMSF_1 in the source table, diameters 27.6 and 27.7 mm). LECAPs are porous expanded-clay ceramic particles rather than thin-walled hollow spheres; particle size range 2.5-3.0 mm, mean not stated. Brittle fracture at very low deflection (~2 mm).

extraction_notes:
Three records: one per specimen configuration (bare MMSF, foam-filled tube, adhesive-bonded foam-filled tube). All share the same syntactic foam composition and the same three-point bend test condition; the 12 individual specimens are replicates, so properties are only published as per-type averages (Table 2) and are entered once per type.

Particle type: the filler is Liapor lightweight expanded clay aggregate (LECAP), a porous/cellular expanded-clay ceramic granule (~60 wt% SiO2, ~17 wt% Al2O3, ~14 wt% Fe2O3), mapped to 'ceramic_hollow' as the closest enum; it is not a thin-walled hollow microsphere, so treat the classification with care.

Nulls: particle volume/weight fraction, particle true density, wall-thickness ratio and mean diameter are not reported in this paper (the filler was characterised in ref. [27]). Only the sieved size range 2.5-3.0 mm is given, so particle_mean_diameter_um is left null rather than assuming a midpoint. No modulus is reported. Strain at failure is left null: the paper reports deflections (e.g. bare MMSF fractures at ~2 mm deflection), not strains.

Energy absorption: Table 2 reports absorbed energy in joules at 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 mm deflection (f-MMSF: 29, 91, 136, 143, 144 J; f-EMMSF: 36, 107, 139, 145, 148 J; MMSF: 6 J at all deflections; ET: 23, 61, 102, 142, 179 J). These are total absorbed energies for a bend specimen, not volumetric MJ/m3, and cannot be converted without an assumed deformed volume, so energy_absorption_mj_m3 is left null.

Density: measured_density_g_cc is set to the study-wide foam-core average of 1.48 +/- 0.05 g/cm3 explicitly stated in Sec. 2.2; individual specimen and core densities from Table 1 are listed in microstructure_notes. Note that Table 1 labels both bare-foam specimens 'MMSF_1' (densities 1.42 and 1.60 g/cm3); the second is presumably MMSF_2.

Process temperature: left null because the paper gives a range rather than a single value - crucible and LECAPs preheated at 600 C for >=30 min, AlSi7Mg heated to ~850 C, and the melt poured and infiltrated at 750-800 C under 500 kPa argon pressure.

Test temperature: not stated; set to 25 C on the standard room-temperature assumption for these quasi-static laboratory bend tests.

Excluded: the empty AlMgSi0.5 tube reference specimens (ET, flexural strength 90 +/- 1 MPa, Fmax 4064 +/- 90 N, 179 J at 25 mm) contain no hollow particles and are not a syntactic foam composition, so no record was created for them. Literature values cited in the introduction (refs. [9], [14], [16], [24], [25], [26]) are qualitative or percentage comparisons with no extractable absolute property values, so no secondary records were created.

Evidence quotes from Table 2 are reconstructed across the line-per-cell layout of the extracted text (the source file lists each cell on its own line) and use 'sigma_b' and '+/-' for the sigma and plus-minus characters.
